teile.name: Hook
teile.text: Their first motorcycle couldn't climb a hill. Harley-Davidson's first machine needed pedals on Milwaukee's hills.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game style: a young man in early 1900s clothes pedals hard up a steep Milwaukee street on a crude motorized bicycle, engine sputtering, medium shot, warm morning light.

teile.name: Reaction
teile.text: But they didn't quit. They called it a valuable learning experiment and started over.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game style: the blue-eyed presenter in fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch stands in a 1900s workshop beside three young men studying an engine, medium shot, lamplight.

teile.name: Bigger engine
teile.text: Harley and the Davidsons built a 405 cc engine in a backyard shed.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game style: three young men in early 1900s work clothes assemble a large engine on a loop-frame motorcycle inside a small wooden backyard shed, wide shot, golden afternoon light.

teile.name: First race
teile.text: Outboard pioneer Ole Evinrude helped. In 1904, it finished fourth in a Milwaukee race.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game style: a rider on an early loop-frame motorcycle races other riders on a dusty 1904 fairground track, spectators in period clothes behind, dynamic low-angle shot, bright daylight.

teile.name: First sales
teile.text: Did anyone buy it? A Chicago dealer sold three of the five shed-built bikes.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game style: a 1905 Chicago dealer in a waistcoat shows a motorcycle to curious customers in a small shop, the presenter in fedora watching from the doorway, medium shot, soft window light.

teile.name: Payoff
teile.text: Harley-Davidson made 16,284 machines in 1914. That hill-stalled start led to racing dominance.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game style: rows of finished motorcycles outside a large five-story brick factory around 1914, the fedora-wearing presenter with gold pocket watch in the foreground, wide shot, golden light.

teile.name: Call to action
teile.text: Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game style: the fedora-wearing presenter stands beside a vintage motorcycle at the top of a Milwaukee hill, city below, gesturing toward the view, medium shot, sunset light.

entwurf.beschreibung: Harley-Davidson's first motorcycle couldn't climb Milwaukee's hills without pedals. The founders learned from it, built a bigger engine, and grew production to 16,284 machines by 1914.
